explanation: User account breach detected -- unauthorized or anomalous access to user accounts. MECHANISM REBUILT FROM REAL SOURCE (2026-08-28): the actual continuous detector is /athinio/bin/secOpsScript_113_bkp, a daemon that tails /var/log/secure live. It's a genuine TWO-STAGE detector, not a simple brute-force pattern: Stage 1 (after a 14-day per-user baseline period) flags a login as merely SUSPICIOUS -- either a brand-new user, or an existing user logging in >=4 hours outside their established earliest-login/last-logout baseline -- and sets alertlog.xml's suspicious_user_login=1 only. Stage 2 watches for 'Failed password'/'authentication failure' lines for that SAME user; if >=3 failed attempts land within a 30-minute window of the suspicious login, it escalates to User_breach=1. A separate wrapper script, /athinio/bin/secOpsScript_113 (no _bkp suffix), manages the daemon (starts/stops it, ensures it's running) and handles admin actions -- locking breached users' accounts (lock_breached_users via param_cmd_113.xml), and both operator-triggered and automatic 24-hour ignore/reset (an unaddressed breach alert self-clears after 24h with no operator response, same pattern as config_drift's auto-expiry). Critically, this wrapper's own secOpsOutput_113 output is NOT independent evidence -- it just reads back the CURRENT User_breach tag value and writes it as a human-readable line ('Info : No user breach detected' / 'Attack : User Breach detected'), the exact same restated-conclusion problem found and fixed in gateway_breach_activity. Do not treat secOpsOutput_113 as corroboration.

known_patterns.pattern: sshd\[\d+\]:\s+Failed password for (?:invalid user )?\S+ from (?P<ip>\d{1,3}(?:\.\d{1,3}){3}).*?sshd\[\d+\]:\s+Accepted password for \S+ from (?P=ip)
known_patterns.meaning: Found failed password attempts followed by a successful password login from the same source address.

evidence_sources.default_meaning: No matching pattern found in the available logs.

metadata.writer_script: /athinio/bin/secOpsScript_113_bkp (real continuous detector, tails var/log/secure) -- managed/reported by /athinio/bin/secOpsScript_113 (wrapper: admin lock/unlock, ignore/auto-ignore reset, restates the tag to secOpsOutput_113)
metadata.confidence: verified -- both scripts' real source read directly
metadata.caveat: TAG SOURCE CORRECTED (2026-08-28): status_file moved from Alert.xml to athinio/system/alertlog.xml, because suspicious_user_login -- a real, currently-active signal on the real test hierarchy -- does not roll up to Alert.xml at all (confirmed absent from its 41-tag schema); alertlog.xml is the only place both tags exist. EVIDENCE QUALITY FIX: secOpsOutput_113 was previously treated as a 'supplementary source' cross-check, but its real source (secOpsScript_113, the wrapper) shows it only restates the current User_breach tag value as text -- it is not independent evidence and has been removed as a cross-check for the same reason gateway_breach_activity's secOpsOutput_105 was retired from that role. MECHANISM GAP: the check_raw_logs regex this workflow actually runs (SSHD_FAIL_RE/SSHD_ACCEPT_RE -- a failed-then-accepted-password-from-the-same-IP pattern) is a DIFFERENT, simpler heuristic than the real two-stage algorithm above. The real algorithm is inherently stateful (a 14-day per-user baseline in user_sessions.xml, per-user failed-attempt counters in athinio/system/failed_logins/, a 30-minute escalation window) and can't be faithfully reproduced by a stateless fresh-scan-of-the-raw-log check. The current regex check is kept as a secondary, approximate signal -- real brute-force activity it catches is still worth flagging -- but it should not be presented as verifying the product's actual mechanism, only as an independent heuristic that happens to look for a related pattern.
